prompt: A loading ramp is $20$ ft long (that is the slanted surface) and rises at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the ground. How high above the ground is the top end of the ramp, in feet?
hint: The ramp is the hypotenuse and the height is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle. Opposite and hypotenuse means sine.

hints.text: The ramp is the hypotenuse and the height is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle. Opposite and hypotenuse means sine.
Write $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{h}{20}$, then multiply both sides by 20.

explanation: The slanted ramp is the hypotenuse ($20$ ft) and the height $h$ sits opposite the $30^\circ$ angle.

alternativeExplanations.title: The half-the-hypotenuse shortcut
steps: In any right triangle with a $30^\circ$ angle, the side opposite that angle is exactly half the hypotenuse.
Half of $20$ ft is $10$ ft, no calculator needed.
